--- title: "XGBoost predictions straight from SQL" description: "Build an XGBoost in R and have SQL generate the predictions with one line of code using {tidypredict}." date: 2020-08-29 author: "Athos Damiani" categories: ["tutorials", "sql", "xgboost", "machine learning"] image: xgboost-sql.webp --- What you'll learn to do by the end of this post is: That is, once you have an XGBoost model fitted in your R, you can ask {tidypredict} to generate the SQL query that would compute the score. PS: the XGBoost in the gif has 2 trees. ### Reasons to use it If there is a very powerful SQL server (or cluster, etc), the prediction can be done directly inside the database, with no need for other tools. Also, putting it into production will be a CTRL+C/CTRL+V away =P. ### The XGBoost predictor The value predicted by XGBoost is, deep down, a sum of CASE WHEN's (or IF ELSE's). The number of trees defines how many CASE WHEN's will be added up. The predictor of an XGBoost with 2 trees would look like this in SQL: ``` 0.0 + CASE WHEN ((`dose` < 5.0 OR ((`dose`) IS NULL))) THEN (-1.95000005) WHEN (`dose` >= 14.0 AND `dose` >= 5.0) THEN (-1.6500001) WHEN ((`dose` < 10.0 OR ((`dose`) IS NULL)) AND (`dose` < 14.0 OR ((`dose`) IS NULL)) AND `dose` >= 5.0) THEN (1.05000007) WHEN (`dose` >= 10.0 AND (`dose` < 14.0 OR ((`dose`) IS NULL)) AND `dose` >= 5.0) THEN (1.35000002) END + CASE WHEN ((`dose` < 5.0 OR ((`dose`) IS NULL))) THEN (-1.36500013) WHEN (`dose` >= 14.0 AND `dose` >= 5.0) THEN (-1.15499997) WHEN ((`dose` < 10.0 OR ((`dose`) IS NULL)) AND (`dose` < 14.0 OR ((`dose`) IS NULL)) AND `dose` >= 5.0) THEN (0.734999955) WHEN (`dose` >= 10.0 AND (`dose` < 14.0 OR ((`dose`) IS NULL)) AND `dose` >= 5.0) THEN (0.945000052) END + 0.5 ``` ### Minimal code The true hero of the code below is the line `tidypredict_sql(xgb_fit$fit, con)` from the [`{tidypredict}`](https://tidypredict.tidymodels.org/) package, which takes the fitted XGBoost object and returns the SQL query with the CASE WHEN's. #### Fitting the XGBoost with {tidymodels} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidymodels) library(tidypredict) library(xgboost) # data ----------------------------------------------------- data <- tibble( dose = c(2, 8, 12, 18), eficacia = c(-6, 4, 5, -5) ) # model specification ------------------------------------- xgb_model <- boost_tree(min_n = 1, trees = 2 ) %>% set_engine("xgboost", lambda = 0) %>% set_mode("regression") # model fit ---------------------------------------------- xgb_fit <- fit(xgb_model, eficacia ~ dose, data = data) # Connection to the SQL database -------------------------- con <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "meu_sqlite_db.db") # Transcribing XGBoost to SQL ----------------------------- tidypredict_sql(xgb_fit$fit, con) ## (CASE ## WHEN (`dose` < 15.0 OR (`dose` IS NULL)) THEN -1.6500001 ## ELSE -1.95000005 ## END + CASE ## WHEN (`dose` < 10.0 OR (`dose` IS NULL)) THEN 0.734999955 ## ELSE 0.945000052 ## END) + 0.5 ``` ::: #### Using {dplyr} to run code in SQL ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # just uploading the data to the SQL database -------- copy_to(con, data, "data", overwrite = TRUE) # Creating the `pred` column with the SQL predictions data_sql <- tbl(con, "data") %>% mutate( pred = !!tidypredict_sql(xgb_fit$fit, con) ) # result ---------------------------------------------- data_sql ## # Source: SQL [4 x 3] ## # Database: sqlite 3.51.2 [C:\Users\ap_da\athosdamiani\posts\2020-08-29-xgboost-sql\meu_sqlite_db.db] ## dose eficacia pred ## ## 1 2 -6 -0.415 ## 2 8 4 -0.415 ## 3 12 5 -0.205 ## 4 18 -5 -0.505 ``` ::: PS: the `tidypredict_sql()` function returns a string, so we use the `!!` operator to interpret it as literal R code. This part can be confusing because dplyr will take the code and turn it into the literal, but it **won't** run the code in R, it will translate from R to SQL directly (and that's why it works, because the string isn't valid R code =P). #### SQL behind the scenes The `data_sql` table generated above by {dplyr} is actually an SQL query. The `show_query()` function shows the resulting translation: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} show_query(data_sql) ## ## SELECT ## `data`.*, ## (CASE ## WHEN (`dose` < 15.0 OR (`dose` IS NULL)) THEN -1.6500001 ## ELSE -1.95000005 ## END + CASE ## WHEN (`dose` < 10.0 OR (`dose` IS NULL)) THEN 0.734999955 ## ELSE 0.945000052 ## END) + 0.5 AS `pred` ## FROM `data` ``` ::: ## Summary - XGBoost to SQL is as simple as one line of code: `tidypredict_sql(xgb_fit$fit, con)` - The SQL query can be used inside `mutate()` with `!!` - XGBoost predictions are no rocket science, they are simple sums of CASE WHEN's. ### Appendix: the two trees ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(DiagrammeR) xgb.plot.tree(model=xgb_fit$fit) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: :::
